question: The Commission recently disclosed via a response to an access to documents request that it cost EUR 28 520 to project the Israeli flag onto the facade of the Berlaymont building (Brussels) in October 2023. The framework contract order form for this projection was signed on the evening of 7 October, less than 24 hours after the Hamas attack of that date. 1.

Given the extremely short time period involved in the decision to award this contract, can the Commission confirm that correct tendering and procurement procedures were followed in full before the contract was signed?
Which budget line was the EUR 28 500 paid out from, and is the Commission satisfied that value for money was obtained?

The final date of delivery of the contract is listed as ‘TBD’ on the form, however the flag projection was in operation just hours after the contract was signed. Is it normal procedure and best practice to issue a contract with no date for delivery listed?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.6.2024) 1. The Commission used for the projection a specific contract based on an already existing framework contract (OIB/2022/OP/00031). The framework contract2 was subject to a tender procedure ensuring the best quality-price ratio. The deliverable in question required a simple specific contract (also known as an order form).

When executing the concerned expenditures under the contract, the Commission respected the principles of sound financial management laid down in Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2018/1046 on the implementation of the EU budget3. 2. The costs of the projection were covered by the budget line designated for visual communication activities, including illuminations, namely budget line BGUE-B202307.200402.
07 ‘Executive and corporate communication services’. The requested services were delivered in accordance with the provisions of the framework contract and in line with the specific contract. 3.

The final date of delivery was exceptionally listed as ‘TBD’ (to be determined) due to the fact that the specific contract was an urgent request and the exact time of delivery could not be indicated with precision when launching the signature procedure.
However, the description of services to be provided by the contractor, included in the specific contract, clearly indicated the date for the illumination which was the date of delivery.
1 https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/462631-2022 2 Article 2.1 (31) of the Financial Regulation defines a framework contract as ‘a public contract concluded

between one or more economic operators and one or more contracting authorities, the purpose of which is to establish the terms governing specific contracts under it to be awarded during a given period, in particular with regard to price and, where appropriate, the quantity envisaged.’ 3 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32018R1046
